page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance provisioned on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an AWS Graviton2 processor using the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs, completely avoiding simultaneous multithreading overhead. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, providing an even 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. A key feature of the instance is its dense bundled storage, consisting of a 3750 GB local NVMe SSD. For network communications, the instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier throughput for core execution and throughput workloads alongside identifiable limits on single-core instruction processing. Multi-core performance is stable, with multi-core Geekbench achieving 5430.0 and stress-ng multi-core reaching 12131.82. In-memory operations show reliable execution, evidenced by Redis SET operations recording 9.97 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring 5226.37. Large uncached read bandwidth measures 121.23 GB/s, while uncached write bandwidth settles at 54.16 GB/s. In contrast, single-threaded processing presents relative constraints: single-core Geekbench scores 937.0, bzip3 single-threaded decompression registers in the bottom decile at 7.19 GB/s, and LLM text generation remains low across smaller models.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of dedicated ARM cores and massive high-speed NVMe storage delivers strong resource density without requiring external block storage overhead. The absence of hardware acceleration hardware such as GPUs, coupled with weaker single-threaded compute output, makes the instance unsuitable for heavy compute-bound mathematical modeling or vector processing. Instead, the balance of substantial local disk capacity, 12 Gbps network baseline, and mid-range multi-core efficiency makes it well aligned for I/O-intensive workloads, including distributed NoSQL databases, log ingestion, search indexing, and real-time cache nodes.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is a storage-optimized Nitro-based instance configured with an 8-core AWS Graviton2 ARM processor running at 2.5 GHz. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps. A central hardware characteristic is the bundled 3750 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering high-capacity, low-latency disk storage without requiring attached volumes. Benchmark results demonstrate balanced multi-core throughput, recording 12131.82 in stress-ng and 9.97 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core compute and compression metrics trend lower. Without an attached GPU or x86 instruction extensions, compute capabilities favor concurrent operational tasks rather than intensive single-threaded processing. The instance serves distributed database nodes, transactional datastores, log indexing, and caching layers requiring extensive local disk space.
